m2c/tests/policy/policy_helpers.py -- Patch C06: shared builders for the policy tests.

Everything is data: a project root and home directory that are plain strings
(nothing is created on disk unless a test says so), rule layers built from
rule strings, and a ``run`` helper that calls ``decide`` once.  No real secret
shapes appear anywhere in these tests: they only name paths.

Place this file at: m2c/tests/policy/policy_helpers.py

m2c/tests/policy/test_policy_decide_table.py -- Patch C06: the large table.

Three tables, all through ``decide``:

* SHELL: bypass attempts and plain commands against a fixed rule set (BASIC:
  a few explicit allows, a few denies, one ask) or a writers rule set.
* FILES: the file tools in each mode, paths that escape or are protected.
* MODES: the same calls in plan, ask and accept-edits.

A row is ``(command_or_input, expected_action)`` with the rule set named by the
table.  The expected action is the point: an ``allow`` only where the rules say
so, ``deny`` for what a rule or the protected/secret lists forbid, ``ask`` for
everything the engine cannot be sure of.  Some rows were seeded from MiniLocker
54520a2 (tests/test_policy.py); they are marked ``# ML``.

m2c/tests/policy/test_policy_interact.py -- Patch L01a: what C06 decides for ``ask_user`` and ``tasks``.

Neither tool touches a file or runs a command, so both are risk R0 in the catalog and the engine allows them in
every mode with no approval prompt (``ask_user`` IS the prompt).  Everything else the engine does still holds:
a deny rule wins, an ask rule asks, malformed input is denied, nothing is auto-allowed when the settings could
not be read, and a risk above R0 asks.

m2c/tests/policy/test_policy_invariants.py -- Patch C06: "no allow without a rule or a mode".

Done-when item: *no code path allows without an explicit rule or mode.*  Three
independent checks:

1. STATIC.  Read decide.py and list every place the string "allow" can be turned
   into a verdict.  Exactly two functions may create an allow verdict
   (``_allow_rule``, ``_allow_mode``) and ``_finalize`` may only compare it; the
   module-level rank table is the only other mention.  A new allow path added
   later fails this test until the test is edited on purpose.
2. EXHAUSTIVE.  modes.mode_default is enumerated over its whole domain
   (test_policy_modes.py); here the engine's own allow paths are enumerated by
   wrapping the two constructors and running thousands of seeded random calls.
   Every Decision that says allow must have been built by one of them, must name
   its basis, and the basis must hold up when recomputed independently.
3. NEGATIVE.  With no allow rule anywhere, shell, delete and plan_exit are never
   allowed in any mode; in plan mode nothing but a read is ever allowed.

The decision function is also shown to be pure: it opens no file, stats nothing,
resolves no symlink, and writes no log.

m2c/tests/policy/test_policy_modes.py -- Patch C06: modes, the tool catalog, risk.

The mode table is checked exhaustively (every mode x tool class x risk x
inside/outside x protected), and the catalog copy in modes.py is checked
against the P00 schemas so that it cannot drift.

m2c/tests/policy/test_policy_review_findings.py -- Patch C06: regression tests for
bypasses found by an independent adversarial review of this patch.

Each case below was reproduced against an earlier revision of the engine (the
engine returned ``allow`` where it must not).  Every row is "allow rule + deny
rule, command, expected action".  Shell-oracle claims ("a real shell would run
curl") were confirmed by the reviewer with bash 5 and a command_not_found_handle
that only logs names.  Backslashes are built with chr(92) so that no escaping
layer can alter them.

m2c/tests/policy/test_policy_robustness.py -- Patch C06: hostile and huge input.

Every input here must come back as a Decision quickly and must never raise.
Anything malformed, unterminated or too complex is ask or deny, never allow, even
under a rule that allows every command.  The time limits are loose (they catch
quadratic or exponential behaviour, not a slow machine).

m2c/tests/policy/test_policy_rules.py -- Patch C06: rules, layers, trust, loading.

Covers rule syntax, matching (exact first, then ``*`` patterns, no regular
expressions), evaluation order deny > ask > allow over the UNION of the layers,
the untrusted-project rule, and the loader (which takes paths as arguments, so
nothing here touches the real home directory, and which fails closed).

m2c/tests/policy/test_policy_shellparse.py -- Patch C06: the shell tokenizer.

Table-driven.  Each row is a command and the commands (parts) the parser must
find in it, in order, written as dequoted text.  The point of the table is that
every way of spelling ``curl`` becomes the word ``curl`` and that every command
hidden inside a substitution, group or wrapper surfaces as a part of its own.
Rows whose reason list is non-empty are "unknown syntax": the engine asks.
